launches.title: Beyond Agents: The Era of AI Employees
launches.body:
Today, StackAI is launching three capabilities that are ushering in the era of AI employees: computer use, access to the web, and the ability to coordinate as a team. Each one is a breakthrough on its own; together, they represent a fundamental shift in what enterprise AI can do.

+++

We’ve moved from AI that responds, to AI that reasons, to AI that acts. Now we’re entering the next stage: AI that works like an employee you onboard. That starts with the same thing you’d give any new team member on day one: a computer, access to your internal tools, and a team to work with.

1. **Giving Every AI Agent a Computer**

Computer use gives each AI agent a sandboxed environment where it can execute commands, run scripts, read and write files, send emails, post Slack messages, and work across the tools your enterprise already uses. Think of it like Claude Code, but living inside StackAI and securely connected to everything your organization already uses.

Video: <https://youtu.be/6fvLqfvqsDg>

Computer Use on StackAI doesn’t just suggest, it reads your repo, runs commands, edits files, and iterates until the job is done. Need a comprehensive performance deck? The agent navigates to your analytics platform, pulls the numbers, builds the charts, then formats everything into a clean, ready-to-share deck and forwards it to your team. Professional output. Zero manual effort. You don’t even have to press send.

These agents reason about what needs to happen, adapt when things change, and find a path to the output regardless of what gets in the way.

**What it Means for Enterprises**

Every knowledge worker spends a significant portion of their time on coordination, data gathering, and repetitive execution. Computer use agents absorb that entire layer, freeing your team to focus on the nuanced work that actually requires human judgment.

2. **Navigating the Web Like a Human Employee**

A huge portion of enterprise work doesn’t happen inside your internal stack. It happens on the web: in vendor portals, legacy systems, government databases, and SaaS platforms that predate modern APIs.

Video: <https://youtu.be/JKyN2mYj72A>

Browser use gives AI agents the ability to navigate the web the way a human does—not through an API or pre-built connector, but by seeing a page, understanding what’s on it, and interacting with it. Clicking, filling forms, logging in, extracting data, submitting inputs. For an agent with browser use, every website is a potential integration; every legacy system, regardless of age or architecture, becomes part of the automation surface.

**What it Means for Enterprises**

Traditional automation has always had a hard boundary: no API, no integration. Enterprises worked around this by having humans manually bridge the gaps. 

But now, an AI employee can log into your logistics vendor’s portal, pull open order status, and update your internal tracking system without anyone touching it. It can monitor competitor pricing across a dozen sites and flag changes before your next pricing review. It can navigate regulatory databases, extract relevant filings, and route them to your compliance team.

Anything a human can do in a browser, an AI employee can do too, including the long tail of irregular, one-off tasks that are too infrequent to build traditional automation around but too time-consuming to keep handing to people.

3. **Coordinating at Scale with Sub-Agent Teams**

Computer use gives AI agents a workstation. Browser use gives them reach across the web. But there’s a ceiling to what any single agent, or any single AI employee, can do alone.

A sub-agent workflow has a manager and a team. The orchestrator agent receives a high-level objective, breaks it into component tasks, delegates each to a specialized sub-agent, reviews the outputs, and synthesizes everything into a final deliverable. Each sub-agent maintains its own context window, so the system handles complex tasks without the constraints that limit a single model.

Take a market intelligence agent. A single agent would need to research competitors, extract financial data, analyze trends, and write everything up sequentially, based on the user’s request. A multi-agent team handles it differently: the orchestrator delegates research to one agent, data extraction to another, analysis to a third, writing to a fourth. Sub-agents may or may not be called upon depending on the original task. The result is one polished deliverable, produced in a fraction of the time.

## **The Era of AI Employees Is Here**

Multi-agent architectures on StackAI let you build workflows that match the actual complexity of your business, not simplified versions of it. 

The era of AI employees is here! Ready to put them to work? 

**Get started with StackAI → [stack-ai.com/demo](http://stack-ai.com/demo)**

launches.title: StackAI: Enterprise AI Agents in Seconds
launches.tagline: Introducing Auto Agents, a new system that allows you to instantly design, test, and iterate over custom AI agents with enterprise-grade security.
launches.body:
**StackAI** is the no-code, drag-and-drop platform to build and deploy enterprise AI agents that automate manual work across every vertical. 

We’re excited to introduce Auto Agents, a suite of tools within the StackAI platform that makes it incredibly easy to design, iterate, and optimize agents automatically. These tools will empower enterprise users of all technical skill levels to create reliable, robust AI agents for any business process. Whether you're in finance, legal, HR, support, or any other department, you’ll be able to take those painful, repetitive, and expensive processes and automate them at scale with AI. \
\
Check out this brief [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ohDG3oeFsjk) to see Auto Agents in action. 

### **From idea to agent in minutes**

With StackAI Auto Agents, teams can describe what they want to build in natural language, and the platform generates a complete, multi-step AI agent automatically.

For example, a user might ask the system to create an equity research agent—one that analyzes stock performance, scans recent news, evaluates opportunities, and produces a structured report. The platform will then design the agent end to end, assembling the workflow, tools, and logic required to complete the task.

Crucially, Auto Agents don’t operate as black boxes. Every generated agent can explain itself, walking users through each component of the workflow, how inputs flow through processing steps, and how outputs are produced. This makes it easier for teams to understand, validate, and build confidence in what the agent is doing.

**Built-in prompt refinement, without the guesswork**

Prompting remains one of the biggest barriers to reliable AI systems. Auto Agents address this directly.

Users can refine an agent’s behavior by describing how outputs should be structured, whether that’s a multi-section research report, a compliance summary, or a decision memo. With a single click, Auto Agents optimize prompts immediately, applying best practices to improve clarity, consistency, and performance.

**Test, iterate, and build on results in real time**

Once an agent is generated, teams can test it right away with real inputs. In the equity research example above, the agent can be run against a specific company, pulling in relevant financial data and recent news to generate a comprehensive report in minutes.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=96563&key=user_uploads/660940/f66c0dcc-f5c7-4f6b-bcdb-bbe33b7ee321)

From there, users can interact directly with the results: asking follow-up questions, extending outputs, or generating downstream artifacts like emails or summaries. This interactive loop allows teams to iterate quickly and build layered workflows on top of existing results, all within the same platform.

**Ready for real enterprise workflows**

Auto Agents are designed for teams automating real business processes, not just demos. This launch reflects a broader shift in enterprise AI to systems that operate reliably at scale across the entire development lifecycle: 

* **Automatic agent generation** from natural language descriptions
* **AI-powered prompt refinement** for better performance
* **Real-time testing and iteration**
* **Interactive follow-ups** through chat-based enhancements
* **Enterprise-grade security and governance** by default

Whether you're automating equity research, streamlining contract reviews, handling RFP responses, or tackling compliance audits, Auto Agents puts the power of AI automation in your hands.

StackAI Auto Agents are available now. To learn more or start building, visit [stack.ai](http://stack.ai).

We do the **heavy lifting of AI and software development so customers can focus on deploying AI that drives business value**.

We also have data processing agreements with leading AI models.
2. **High-touch customer success:** We support each client along the journey, guaranteeing hands-on guidance when building and deploying AI projects. 
3. **Dedicated infrastructure:** We ensure optimal performance and privacy in our client applications.
4. **All-in-one platform:** Our versatile platform allows companies to deploy multiple customized use cases in an all-in-one platform, **simplifying technology stack and vendor management**.

[Learn more about AI for the enterprise](https://www.stack-ai.com/solutions/ai-agents)
